Secure & Sustainable AI Systems

Measuring what it costs to make AI secure, from battery-powered sensors to cloud services.

Research Description

Overview

How much energy and time does an AI system need to stay reliable under attack? We study accuracy, robustness, energy use, latency, and estimated carbon emissions together. Our work ranges from model pruning on sensing devices to the resource costs of training and defending machine learning models.

Research Thrusts

Resource-aware resilience

Measure when attacks increase the cost of processing inputs and whether defenses preserve accuracy within energy and latency budgets.

Efficient learning and deployment

Compare how model size, hardware, and workload shape the costs of training and inference, especially on resource-constrained devices.

Emerging AI infrastructure

Explore how AI agents and data-center workloads can meet security, power, and response-time constraints as computation shifts between edge and cloud.

Research Goals

Identify when a defense improves robustness without exceeding a device’s energy budget or delaying a time-critical response.

Intellectual Merit

Separate the costs introduced by an attack or defense from those explained by the model, hardware, and workload.

Research Impact

Help researchers and engineers choose defenses that meet both security requirements and real resource limits.

Selected Studies & Emerging Work

IEEE GLOBECOM 2025

Resource-aware adversarial resilience

Sensing workload→Attack / defense→Accuracy + energy + latency

An attack can slow a sensing model and raise its energy use even when the predicted activity label does not change.

Research objectives

Test whether model pruning reduces excess energy use and delay while retaining useful predictions.

Approach & Intellectual Merit

Our sensing-AI study compares accuracy, energy, and latency to show where an accuracy-only evaluation misses a vulnerability.

Selected publications

Sponge attacks on sensing ai: Energy-latency vulnerabilities and defense via model pruning ↗

Research Relevance

Battery-powered sensors and edge devices need to keep responding under attack, not merely make correct predictions in a benchmark.

Published Research

Sustainable machine learning

Training & defense→Measure resource use→Explain tradeoffs

Training and testing a model against adversarial examples can add to its energy requirements. That cost belongs in the evaluation of the defense.

Research objectives

Compare the resource and environmental costs of training and defending models under stated hardware and energy assumptions.

Approach & Intellectual Merit

Our studies examine the costs of adversarial training and how to estimate emissions from machine learning workloads.

Selected publications

Selected sustainability publications ↗

Research Relevance

Reporting which stages are included and how electricity use is translated into estimated emissions makes results easier to compare across studies.

Emerging Direction

AI infrastructure and agent systems

Devices & agents→Edge / cloud coordination→Security + resource budgets

When agents hand work off across devices and cloud services, moving computation can shift where delay, energy use, and security risks arise.

Research objectives

Study how to allocate computing resources and pass evidence between agents without weakening security checks.

Approach & Intellectual Merit

Compare whole workflows so an apparent saving at one component does not hide extra computation or communication elsewhere.

Research Relevance

The design question is where to run a task and its security checks when devices, networks, and servers have different constraints.
